- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.67), as models tend to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near zero (sentiment < 0.33), as models fail to capture bearish momentum.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if forecast is high and true price drops sharply within 3–5 days, reduce future forecasts by 2–5% to account for momentum decay.
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after recent price peaks — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below the immediate prior high if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–1.00), reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term sentiment swings.
- If true price drops below 10% of recent 5-day average, adjust forecast downward by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion bias.
- Forecast should not exceed 15% above the 30-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.85) and recent price action confirms breakout.
